html:
SMTO-EML-0008 — Your mail server refused to accept the message

GUID: e8f7d3bc-22db-5262-9a8d-d90d60ee7821
Slug: email-data-rejected
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The mail server accepted the recipients but then refused the message itself, for example because of its content, size or a sending limit. The server did not accept it for delivery.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details and note the mail server's response code. A code starting with 4 is a temporary refusal; one starting with 5 is permanent. The code tells you whether waiting will help or the message itself must change.
  2. For a temporary refusal, wait for any sending limit to reset. For a permanent one, remove unusual links or attachments, or shorten the message. Mail servers refuse messages that break their sending limits or content rules.
  3. Ask your email administrator whether the mailbox hit a sending limit or a content rule, and what the mail server's records say. Only the mail server's owner can see the full reason for the refusal.
  4. Before sending again, check the sender mailbox's Sent folder (if your provider keeps one), or ask a recipient, whether the email arrived. Then ask SMTO to send the corrected email. Checking first makes sure recipients don't get a second copy.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details, which include the server's response code, and send them to your email administrator. Don't send the same message again and again; repeated attempts can trigger more limits or spam blocks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The SMTP server rejected the DATA command with a non-354 reply, or returned a final 4xx or 5xx rejection after receiving the message content.

What this means

  • SMTP rejects the DATA command with a non-354 reply or returns a final 4xx/5xx rejection after the message bytes. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • SMTP rejects the DATA command with a non-354 reply or returns a final 4xx/5xx rejection after the message bytes.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether refusal preceded body transmission or followed it and retain the numeric final reply.

How to fix it

  • Read smtp_response_code and last_confirmed_stage (DATA_COMMAND or FINAL_DATA_REPLY_RECEIVED) in the send result and match them to the provider's policy (4xx temporary, 5xx permanent; rate limits, content or spam filtering, size). Resolve the rejection with the mail administrator before resending.
  • Review server message policy and the numeric SMTP response. Resend only after resolving the rejection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The server policy cause is resolved and any later authorized send follows the original known rejection evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
